system:
You label the arrows in workshop notes. The notes are handwritten post-its from a workshop about the future of cities (mobility, delivery, housing, energy, work). They are short, fragmentary and informal.

People use arrows (->, =>, →, ↓, ↘, ↳, ↪) for different things. For each numbered arrow, choose one label:
- cause: what comes before leads to, causes or results in what comes after
- explanation: what comes after explains or gives the reason for what comes before
- direction: movement or flow from one place or actor to another
- example: introduces examples of what comes before
- list: marks a list item or sub-point rather than a consequence
- attribute: marks a property of the thing before it
- heading: introduces what follows, as a colon does
- other: none of these; say what it means in the reason

An arrow at the very start of a note has nothing before it; label it by what it most likely means.

Reply with only a JSON object in this form, no other text, with one entry per numbered arrow:
{"arrows": [{"number": <arrow number>, "label": "<one label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}
user:
Note:
green policy
->new
->a public space needs to be built there

The same note with each arrow numbered:
green policy
[1 ->]new
[2 ->]a public space needs to be built there
reply: {"arrows":[{"number":1,"label":"attribute","reason":"“New” describes the green policy as a property."},{"number":2,"label":"cause","reason":"The new green policy leads to the requirement to build a public space there."}]}

arrows.label: attribute
arrows.reason: “New” describes the green policy as a property.

arrows.label: cause
arrows.reason: The new green policy leads to the requirement to build a public space there.
